landmarks.name: Angel Falls
landmarks.writeup: The world's highest uninterrupted waterfall, located in Canaima National Park.

wiki.extract:
Angel Falls  is a waterfall in Venezuela.
It is the world's tallest uninterrupted waterfall, with a height of 979 metres (3,212 ft), and a plunge of 807 m (2,648 ft). The waterfall drops over the edge of the Auyán-tepui mountain in the Canaima National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the Gran Sabana region of Bolívar State. The height figure, 979 m (3,212 ft), mostly consists of the main plunge but also includes about 400 metres (1,300 ft) of sloped cascade and rapids below the drop and then a 30-metre-high (100 ft) plunge downstream of these talus rapids.

landmarks.name: Mérida Cable Car
landmarks.writeup: The longest and highest cable car in the world, offering panoramic views of the Andes.

wiki.extract: The Mérida Cable Car is a cable car system in Venezuela. Its base is located in the Venezuelan city of Mérida at an altitude of 1,577 metres (5,174 ft), and its terminus is on Pico Espejo, at 4,765 metres (15,633 ft). It is the highest and second longest cable car in the world. The system was opened to the public in 1960, and closed in 2008 for reconstruction. In October 2016, a new regular service was inaugurated.

landmarks.name: Los Roques Archipelago
landmarks.writeup: A national park known for its pristine beaches and rich marine biodiversity.

wiki.extract: The Los Roques Archipelago is a federal dependency of Venezuela consisting of approximately 350 islands, cays, and islets in a total area of 40.61 km2 (15.68 mi2). The archipelago is located 128 km (80 mi) directly north of the port of La Guaira, in the Caribbean Sea.

landmarks.name: Plaza Bolívar
landmarks.writeup: Historic central square in Caracas named after Simón Bolívar, the country's liberator.

wiki.extract: Bolívar Square in Caracas is one of the most important and recognized Venezuelan public spaces. It is located in the center of the first 25 blocks of Caracas when it was founded as "Santiago de León de Caracas" in 1567. It is in the historic center of the city in the Cathedral Parish of the Libertador Municipality.

landmarks.name: Morrocoy National Park
landmarks.writeup: A coastal park famous for its cays, coral reefs, and diverse wildlife.

wiki.extract: Morrocoy National Park lies on the east coast of Falcón State and the north-west side of Golfo Triste, on the west central Venezuelan coast, near the towns of Boca de Aroa, Tucacas, Sanare, Chichiriviche, and Tocuyo de la Costa. It was declared a national park on 26 May 1974. The park's wildlife has suffered from human activity, and there has been a significant decline in coral species in recent years.

cultural_events.name: Carnaval
cultural_events.writeup: A vibrant pre-Lenten festival featuring parades, music, and dancing across the country.

cultural_events.name: Feria de la Chinita
cultural_events.writeup: An annual festival in Maracaibo honoring the Virgin of Chiquinquirá with religious and cultural activities.

cultural_events.name: Festival de Teatro de Caracas
cultural_events.writeup: A major theater festival showcasing national and international performances.

food_writeup: Venezuelan cuisine features arepas (cornmeal cakes), pabellón criollo (shredded beef with rice and beans), hallacas (corn dough stuffed with meat), and empanadas, reflecting indigenous, African, and Spanish influences.
brief_history: Originally inhabited by indigenous peoples, Venezuela was colonized by Spain in the 16th century. It gained independence in 1821 under Simón Bolívar. The 20th century saw oil-driven economic growth and political instability. Recent decades have been marked by economic crisis and social challenges.

important_people.name: Hugo Chávez
important_people.description: Former president and leader of the Bolivarian Revolution

current_conflicts: Venezuela faces political and economic crises, including disputes over presidential legitimacy, hyperinflation, shortages of basic goods, and mass migration. International sanctions and internal unrest continue to impact stability.
